stem: You saved two accounts named `open_acct` and `premium_acct` without marking a default, then run `service = QiskitRuntimeService()` with no arguments. According to the documented behavior, which account's credentials are used?

options.text: It raises an error because no default account is set.
The account that was saved last.
`open_acct`, because free (Open) plans always take precedence.
The account whose name comes last alphabetically — here `premium_acct`.
The one whose name sorts first alphabetically — here `open_acct`.
It usually picks the account with the broadest instance access.

explanation.correct: When multiple credential sets are saved, none is marked default, and none is specified at initialization, the service uses the one whose name comes last alphabetically. `premium_acct` sorts after `open_acct`, so `premium_acct` is used.

distractors.A: It does not raise — the alphabetical-last account is selected as the fallback.
distractors.B: Save order is not the tiebreaker; alphabetical name order is.
distractors.C: There is no automatic preference for free (Open) plans when choosing among SAVED named accounts; the alphabetical rule applies.
distractors.E: The rule is real but runs the other way: the account whose name sorts LAST is the one loaded. Half-remembering the direction is the whole trap in this question.
distractors.F: Nothing inspects plans or entitlements when a default is missing. The selection is purely lexicographic over the saved account names.

provenance.notes: meta-pattern fix pass: length/stem-echo/absolute calibration (s4) — removed hedge pile-up from the distractors (avoid-hedged calibration). | pool wave: +E (alphabetically first wins), +F (broadest access wins)
